findings: Frontal (AP) radiograph of the pelvis and lower lumbar spine with both hip joints and proximal femora partly included.
A dense, radiopaque, tapering column of material fills the midline of the pelvis from about the sacral level down toward the perineum, with multiple rounded outpouchings along both margins.
The pattern follows the expected rectosigmoid course and suggests positive contrast (barium-like) within the rectum and sigmoid colon, with haustral or diverticular-type saccular projections.
The lateral outpouchings are numerous and smoothly rounded, with variable size.

A blurred gray rectangular obscuration overlies the inferior midline pelvis and perineum, hiding the lower end of the contrast column. This looks like an image-editing or privacy mask rather than anatomy.
Gas-containing colonic loops are visible in the right abdomen.
Lumbar vertebrae show degenerative-appearing endplate and facet changes.
The bony pelvis and hips are symmetric, with no obvious acute fracture or hip dislocation.
Soft tissue folds are seen laterally.
differential: Barium-opacified rectosigmoid colon with diverticulosis or haustral saccules, as in a barium enema or retained oral contrast
Retained contrast or barium in a redundant sigmoid colon with possible fecal loading
Dense intraluminal material, such as a rectal foreign body or fecal impaction with radiopaque content (less likely given the smooth, contrast-like opacity)
anatomyConcerns: The blurred rectangular patch over the perineum is an artifact or redaction that obscures the distal rectum and anal region, so the inferior extent of the contrast column cannot be assessed.
The bright column is not native bone density. It is an intraluminal radiopaque substance, not impossible anatomy.
No definite impossible anatomy is otherwise seen. The pelvis, spine and hips are in plausible relationships.
